text: The Patriots' offensive woes deepened this week as Greg Van Roten joined the growing list of injured offensive linemen on the shelf, placing added pressure on a unit that's already struggling mightily—New England ranks dead last in the NFL at 9.7 offensive points per game, a damning indictment that extends well beyond injuries. Drake Maye's early-season struggles reached a nadir Sunday in a 35-6 blowout loss to Jacksonville, where he threw two interceptions and lost a fumble while the Jaguars' Trevor Lawrence torched the defense with three touchdown passes, prompting Maye himself to call the offense's performance "unacceptable" as he searches for answers. The questions about whether the Patriots are deploying their young quarterback correctly continue to swirl in film breakdowns and analysis, but this much is certain: the offensive line infrastructure that was supposed to protect him is crumbling just as the unit's overall execution has become indefensible. New England heads to Buffalo on Sunday to face the Bills at Highmark Stadium in Week 4, a contest that will offer another opportunity to determine whether this offensive malaise can be arrested or whether we're witnessing something far more systemic.
